title: Improving the Warehouse Handoff
description: Edit a full informational passage for grammar, punctuation, usage, and clarity.
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewNotes: Mixed editing passage reviewed for sentence-context fidelity, one-best-answer grammar logic, and GED-style editing transfer.

questions.prompt: Choose the parallel revision: “The supervisor records unfinished tasks, equipment problems, and which deliveries are late.”

options.text: The supervisor records unfinished tasks, equipment problems, and late deliveries.
The supervisor records unfinished tasks, problems with equipment, and which deliveries are late.
options.whyWrong: The third item is a clause while the first two are noun phrases.

options.text: The supervisor records unfinished tasks, equipment problems, and identifying late deliveries.
options.whyWrong: The final item changes to a gerund phrase.

options.text: The supervisor records unfinished tasks, equipment problems, and deliveries are late.
options.whyWrong: The final item becomes an independent clause.

explanation.whyCorrect: All three items are parallel noun phrases naming what the supervisor records.
explanation.quickTip: Keep items in a list in matching grammatical forms.

questions.prompt: Choose the best modifier placement: “Supervisors should only use the phone for urgent safety problems.”

options.text: Only supervisors should use the phone for urgent safety problems.
options.whyWrong: This says no one except supervisors may use the phone, which changes the intended limitation.

options.text: Supervisors only should use the phone for urgent safety problems.
options.whyWrong: This awkward placement can imply a contrast with other actions rather than limiting the reason for phone use.

options.text: Supervisors should use the phone only for urgent safety problems.
Supervisors should use only the phone for urgent safety problems.
options.whyWrong: This says the phone is the only tool they may use, not that phone use is limited to urgent problems.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Only' sits directly before the purpose it limits: urgent safety problems.
explanation.quickTip: Place only beside the word or phrase you intend to restrict.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence boundary: “The form is useful {{blank}} it does not replace urgent phone calls.”

options.whyWrong: A comma alone creates a splice between two complete clauses.

options.text: , but
because
options.whyWrong: 'Because' would say the form is useful for the reason that it does not replace calls, which is not the intended contrast.
The second clause is a contrast, not an explanation introduced by a colon.

explanation.whyCorrect: A comma plus 'but' correctly joins the two independent clauses and shows contrast.
explanation.quickTip: Use punctuation and conjunctions together to show the relationship between complete clauses.

questions.prompt: Choose the most concise revision: “The form contains fields that are labeled with labels for routine updates.”

options.text: The form contains fields that are labeled with labels for routine updates.
options.whyWrong: 'Labeled with labels' repeats the same idea.

options.text: The form has fields which have labels that label routine updates.
options.whyWrong: The revision repeats 'label' and remains wordy.

options.text: Routine updates are in fields having labeling labels on the form.
options.whyWrong: This is awkward and less clear.

options.text: The form contains labeled fields for routine updates.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Labeled fields' expresses the same information directly.
explanation.quickTip: Turn repeated noun/verb phrases into one precise modifier when meaning is preserved.

options.text: Supervisors must complete the form before leaving.
Supervisors gotta fill out the form before they leave.
options.whyWrong: 'Gotta' is informal speech and not appropriate for a formal procedure.

options.text: Supervisors should of completed the form before leaving.
Supervisors be completing the form before leaving.
options.whyWrong: This construction is not standard for the intended instruction.

explanation.whyCorrect: The sentence uses clear standard English and states the requirement directly.
explanation.quickTip: Formal procedures should use standard forms without slang or speech spellings.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: “The list of delayed trucks {{blank}} updated before each shift change.”

options.text: are
options.whyWrong: 'Trucks' is inside an of-phrase; the subject is singular 'list'.

options.text: have been
options.whyWrong: This plural verb phrase does not agree with 'list'.

options.text: is
were
options.whyWrong: This plural past-tense verb does not match the singular subject.

explanation.whyCorrect: The singular subject 'list' takes the singular verb 'is'.
explanation.quickTip: Ignore nouns inside an of-phrase when locating the subject.
